hints: Focus on what excess hot concentrated sulfuric acid does to alcohols, think elimination of water to form alkenes.
Work out the starting formula C7H14O2 and notice losing two waters to reach C7H10 means two C=C bonds must form, one in the ring and one exocyclic.
Check symmetry for each diol by asking where the ring double bond can go after the secondary OH leaves, and see which starting material gives identical options.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Both groups in each compound are alcohol groups, one secondary on the ring and one primary as $-CH_2OH$.

Hot excess concentrated $H_2SO_4$ causes dehydration, elimination of $H_2O$ to form $C=C$:
$$R-OH \rightarrow alkene + H_2O$$

**Find the molecular formula change**

Each starting diol is $C_7H_{14}O_2$. Losing two waters gives:
$$C_7H_{14}O_2 - 2H_2O \rightarrow C_7H_{10}$$
So the product must be a diene with one ring still intact. The $-CH_2OH$ becomes an exocyclic $=CH_2$ group, and the ring $-OH$ becomes an endocyclic double bond.

**Test compound 1 for symmetry**

In 1 the two groups are at C1 and C4, opposite each other. The exocyclic double bond can only form at C1 in one way, and the ring double bond at C4 can form toward C3 or C5 which are mirror images. Both routes give the same 4-methylenecyclohex-1-ene, so only one $C_7H_{10}$ product.

**Test compounds 2 and 3 for isomers**

In 2 the groups are adjacent and in 3 they are 1,3 apart. Removing the ring $OH$ can give a ring double bond on either side of that carbon, and those two sides are not symmetric with respect to the $-CH_2$ group. One route gives a conjugated diene and the other gives an isolated diene, so each gives at least two different $C_7H_{10}$ isomers. Therefore only 1 qualifies.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three give a single product. Compounds 2 and 3 each allow the ring double bond to form in two non equivalent positions, giving conjugated and non conjugated diene isomers.
options.B: Correct. Only compound 1 is symmetric enough that dehydration of the secondary alcohol to either adjacent carbon gives the same product, and dehydration of the primary alcohol gives only one exocyclic methylene. It therefore forms only one diene of formula C7H10.
options.C: Incorrect. Compound 2 with adjacent OH and CH2OH groups can eliminate to give different positions for the endocyclic double bond, including methylcyclohexadiene type and methylenecyclohexene type structures, so more than one C7H10 product is possible.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 3 both work. Compound 3 does give C7H10 products but gives two of them because loss of H from C2 versus C4 gives different dienes relative to the exocyclic methylene group.
